newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha weaker, physical deal at $191.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha weaker, physical deal at $191.

text.p: European naphtha swaps fell back by $3-$4 on Monday on the back of a crude futures' slump late Friday, producing an August trade of a 5,000 tonne lot at $186 but few other identifiable trades.

August swaps were placed in the $186-$187 range, down from around $191 just prior to the late Friday crude slump. September naphtha was still valued $3 under August and October around $0.50-$1 behind September.
A late physical cargo deal at $191 CIF NWE, confirmed by the buyer and the broker that put it together, underlined the lower price sentiment.
That contrasted with bid and offer talk at $194-$195 during Friday.
The $191 deal was for a July 26-August 5 shipment of 20,000-25,000 tonnes of pipeline spec naphtha, the broker said.

Several traders expressed surprise at what they still saw as a particularly high-priced trade, contending that the market was no longer as tight as it has been under the influence of an open Med arb to the East and to the U.S. Gulf.

The Med itself saw no real cargo talk or trades Monday as some traders said the Med-Asia arb was now closed, although they acknowleged the arb to the U.S. Gulf could still be worked undfer specific shipment conditions.
